title: Demo deck visual refresh v1: unify templates, icons, and latency/cost visuals
creator: Soojin Lee
body:
## Context
We’re standardizing the Redwood sales demo so every AE/SE run looks consistent and resilient. The deck is the backbone (live demo + backup mode), but v1 drafts have inconsistent chart styles, mixed iconography, and visuals that don’t match Console UI.

This ticket delivers a visual refresh for **redwood-demo-deck v1**: updated slide templates, consistent icon set, and a unified visual language for **latency/cost** ("production economics") and **deployment modes** (Hosted / Dedicated / Private).

## Goals
1) Make the deck look like a coherent product artifact (not stitched slides).
2) Provide repeatable templates so PMM/Sales can edit without breaking layout.
3) Ensure key messages land quickly via consistent visuals:
   - Production economics (latency vs cost, batching/caching/quantization levers)
   - Reliability (fallback routing / graceful degradation)
   - Deployment flexibility (Hosted → Dedicated → Private)
   - Observability (token-level breakdown, traces, rollouts)

## Non-goals
- Creating new narrative/slide order (owned by PMM; we’ll adapt to the existing outline).
- Rebuilding Console UI screenshots (handled in DES-611; we’ll define the style + callout system).

## Deliverables
### A) Updated slide templates (Google Slides / PPT-compatible)
- Title / section divider
- Problem framing + "why now"
- 2-column product overview
- Feature deep dive (left: copy, right: screenshot/diagram)
- Chart slides (latency/cost) with consistent axes & typography
- Architecture slide template (VPC/private) with a small legend + callouts
- Appendix template (security FAQ / procurement)

Template rules:
- 12-column grid, 40px outer margins, consistent spacing scale (8/16/24/32)
- Headline typography: 36/44, subhead: 20/28, body: 14/22
- "Speaker notes safe area" at bottom to avoid cropping in screen share

### B) Iconography system
- Single icon family (outlined, 2px stroke) used across all slides
- Approved set (minimum): latency, cost, shield/security, globe/regions, routing, dashboard/observability, database/logs, key/auth, GPU/capacity
- Usage rules:
  - One accent color max per slide
  - Icons never used as bullets; always paired with a short label

### C) Chart + data-viz standard
Focus: latency vs cost framing without implying guarantees.

1) **Latency distribution** visuals
- Preferred: percentile band chart (p50/p95) with light fill + single accent line
- Default y-axis: milliseconds; avoid log scale in customer-facing decks
- Footnote: "Illustrative; varies by model, sequence length, and region"

2) **Cost breakdown** visuals
- Preferred: stacked bar for per-request cost components (prompt tokens / output tokens / overhead)
- Secondary: "unit economics levers" table with before/after (cache hit rate, batch size)
- Footnote: "Illustrative; pricing/throughput depends on deployment mode"

3) **Tradeoff** visuals
- A single canonical quadrant chart: "Lower latency" vs "Lower cost" with labeled levers:
  - Continuous batching
  - KV/prefix caching
  - Routing policies (cost-aware)
  - Quantization profiles

### D) Latency/cost visuals ("Production economics")
Create 3 reusable diagram components:
1) "Same model, different economics": toggles (batching/caching) → cost/token down, p95 stable
2) Token-level breakdown callout: screenshot annotation style guide (matches Console)
3) Simple ROI equation slide: "Requests/day × tokens/request × $/1M tokens" with placeholders (no hard-coded numbers)

### E) Deployment modes visuals
- A consistent 3-card layout:
  - Hosted API: fastest time-to-value
  - Dedicated: predictable throughput + isolation
  - Private: VPC/on-prem control plane + compliance
- Architecture diagram style:
  - Redwood components in Redwood blue
  - Customer network boundary in neutral gray
  - Data flow arrows consistent (single style)
  - Explicit callout: "Demo uses synthetic data"

### F) Screenshot callout system (shared with DES-611)
- Callout chips: 1–2 words max (e.g., "p95", "fallback", "A/B")
- Numbered callouts if more than 3 annotations
- Redaction pattern: blur + "Synthetic" watermark, never black boxes (looks suspicious)

## Files / links
- Canonical deck outline: sources/confluence/sales-enablement/pitch-decks/redwood-demo-deck-v1.json
- Talk track: sources/confluence/sales-enablement/positioning-and-messaging/demo-talk-track-script-v1.json
- Backup screenshots task: DES-611

## Acceptance criteria
- Deck templates published with a short "How to use" page (1 slide) inside the template deck.
- All v1 slides updated to new style (at least: title, problem, differentiators, production economics, reliability, deployment modes, observability, security appendix).
- No mismatched icon styles; all charts use the approved system.
- Export test: PDF and screen-share readability at 100% zoom.

## Risks / notes
- Avoid any chart that looks like a hard performance commitment. Use "illustrative" footnotes and keep axes unlabeled with absolute values unless PMM explicitly approves.
- Ensure color contrast meets accessibility basics for screen sharing.

## Handoff
Owner for ongoing changes: PMM can duplicate the template; design reviews only needed for new chart types or new diagram families.
comments: 2025-11-11 (Soojin Lee): Creating this from deck review feedback—biggest issues were inconsistent charts and mixed icon sets. Goal is a clean v1 template we can freeze for enablement rollout.
2025-11-12 (Markus Klein): +1. Please keep any performance visuals clearly illustrative; we’ve had prospects treat charts as commitments. Also need layouts that look good on Zoom (no tiny labels).
2025-11-13 (Camila Reyes): Marketing request: keep "Production economics" as headline language but make the visuals less "benchmark-y" and more about control levers + observability proof.
2025-11-15 (Alyssa Chen): Drafted templates + grid. Proposing outlined icon set and a single accent color per slide. Will share v0.3 in #marketing for quick feedback.
2025-11-18 (Soojin Lee): Reviewed v0.3—looks aligned. Request: add a standard footnote component for performance charts (small, consistent placement).

2025-11-20 (Alyssa Chen): Added footnote component + standardized chart styles (percentile band + stacked bars). Created 3-card deployment slide and a VPC boundary diagram template. Ready for DES-611 to drop in updated screenshots with the callout system.
2025-11-25 (Camila Reyes): Final pass approved for v1. Publishing template deck to GTM shared drive and linking from the enablement rollout doc.
